goal.source_text: More downforce without going over 15 N of drag at 25 m/s. You can change the angle, span, flap angle, flap size and endplates. Keep the chord.
assumptions: Chord, airfoil, mounts and ride height stay fixed.

design_space.name: FSAE-style rear wing

parameters.name: chord_mm
parameters.description: Total chord, main element plus flap

parameters.name: flap_chord_frac
parameters.description: Flap chord as a fraction of total chord

notes: Ranges from PLAN.md B.5; W-B owns the real solver and may narrow them before CP-B.

metric_catalog.name: downforce_n
metric_catalog.description: Downforce at the design speed (VLM + viscous correction + endplates)

metric_catalog.name: drag_n
metric_catalog.description: Total drag: induced + section profile + endplate friction

metric_catalog.name: drag_profile_n
metric_catalog.description: Section profile drag (NeuralFoil) plus endplate skin friction

metric_catalog.name: cl
metric_catalog.description: Wing lift coefficient on planform area

metric_catalog.name: stall_margin_deg
metric_catalog.description: Section stall angle minus angle of attack (negative = stalled)

metric_catalog.name: span_efficiency
metric_catalog.description: Oswald e from Prandtl lifting-line theory for the planform

payload.explanation: The combined span and endplate increase was accepted. Downforce rose 15.8%, drag 5.56%, L/D 9.73%, matching predictions. Induced drag unexpectedly grew 0.856% due to 18.2% higher effective aspect ratio not offsetting area increase; profile drag rose 23.3% from larger surface.
payload.lesson: Increasing span and endplates together boosts L/D but can raise induced drag; monitor area effects.

payload.explanation: Reducing flap angle from 15 to 12 deg lowered downforce by 3.08% and drag by 10.7%, with profile drag falling 24.6% and induced drag 6.07%. L/D improved 8.5% and stall margin increased 14.3%. Predictions matched directions but mostly under-predicted magnitudes, so the step was rejected despite beneficial tradeoffs.
payload.lesson: Flap angle near saturation shows larger drag reductions than predicted, improving L/D beyond expectations.

payload.explanation: Increasing angle to 7.0 deg raised downforce 2.08%, but drag rose 5.32%, reducing L/D by 3.09%. Both induced and profile drag increased (4.19% and 8.75%), while stall margin dropped 28.6% to 2.5 deg. Predictions for lower drag and higher L/D were wrong; the added angle mainly increased profile drag, not lift efficiency.
payload.lesson: Above moderate angle, further increases mostly add profile drag and shrink stall margin.

L/D rose 8.44%, exceeding the 0.5-3% prediction. Stall margin improved 20.0%, beyond predicted 5-15%, because flap angle decrease near saturation relieves loading.
payload.lesson: Flap reduction cuts drag more than downforce, improving L/D and stall margin beyond linear expectation.

payload.lesson: Small endplate height changes yield weak effects; effective AR increase alone doesn't boost L/D much.

payload.explanation: The AOA reduction from 7.0 to 6.5 deg matched predictions: downforce fell by 1.059% (within -4.0 to -0.5), drag by 2.655% (within -7.0 to -1.0), and stall margin rose by 20% (to 3.0 deg), clearing the 3 deg target. L/D improved 1.64%. The verdict 'rejected' is unexpected; likely the code rejects because stall margin is still insufficient or a hidden constraint, not because of prediction misses.
payload.lesson: A modest AOA reduction effectively boosts stall margin while minimizing downforce loss.
